theory.intro: Once the sides of a right-angled triangle are named from a chosen angle, each pair of sides can be written as a fraction. Those three fractions are the sine, cosine and tangent ratios of that angle.
facts: A ratio must always name its angle. $\sin\theta$ and $\sin\alpha$ are different fractions in the same triangle, because the opposite and adjacent sides swap.

Given two side lengths, the pair of names tells you which ratio to use: opposite and hypotenuse $\rightarrow$ sine; adjacent and hypotenuse $\rightarrow$ cosine; opposite and adjacent $\rightarrow$ tangent.
steps: Label the sides relative to the marked angle
Write the ratio as a fraction of the two side lengths

foundation.question_text: Write the definition of $\cos\theta$ in terms of the sides of a right-angled triangle.

foundation.solution_text:
The sides are named from $\alpha$, so the adjacent side is the vertical one.
$\cos\alpha$
$=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
$=\dfrac{9}{15}$
$=\dfrac{3}{5}$

The labelled sides are the opposite ($4$) and the hypotenuse ($7$).
Opposite with hypotenuse is the sine ratio.
$\sin\theta$
$=\dfrac{4}{7}$

development.solution_text:
The labelled sides are the adjacent ($9$) and the hypotenuse ($12$).
Adjacent with hypotenuse is the cosine ratio.
$\cos\theta$
$=\dfrac{9}{12}$
$=\dfrac{3}{4}$

The labelled sides are the opposite ($x$) and the adjacent ($6$).
Opposite with adjacent is the tangent ratio.
$\tan\theta$
$=\dfrac{x}{6}$

The sides are named from $\alpha$, so the opposite side is the horizontal one.
$\sin\alpha$
$=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
$=\dfrac{21}{29}$

mastery.solution_text:
The labelled sides are the opposite ($11$) and the adjacent ($12$); the hypotenuse is not given.
Sine and cosine both need the hypotenuse, so only the tangent ratio can be written.
$\tan\theta$
$=\dfrac{11}{12}$

mastery.question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$, $AB=20$, $BC=21$ and $AC=29$. Write $\cos(\angle ACB)$ and $\tan(\angle BAC)$ as fractions.
mastery.solution_text:
The hypotenuse is $AC=29$, opposite the right angle at $B$.
From $\angle ACB$ the adjacent side is $BC=21$.
$\cos(\angle ACB)=\dfrac{21}{29}$
From $\angle BAC$ the opposite side is $BC=21$ and the adjacent side is $AB=20$.
$\tan(\angle BAC)=\dfrac{21}{20}$
